_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); subscription software signals with salesforce.com's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (CRM listed 2004-06-23)

pit_profile.why: 'We are a leading provider of enterprise cloud computing and social enterprise solutions, and are dedicated to helping customers transform themselves into social enterprises.' 'The market for our offerings is highly competitive, rapidly evolving and fragmented, and subject to changing technology, frequent introductions of new products and services, and as we have seen recently, consolidation.' 'The market in which we participate is intensely competitive, and if we do not compete effectively, our operating results could be harmed.' (FY2012 10-K); DURABLE: no 10-K calls the business cyclical ('cycle' appears only as the sales cycle and payment cycles); no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a subscription software company on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': the 10-K names cloud computing as salesforce.com's own model, the side that displaces on-premise software, not a substitute for it, and names no offshore delivery), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

(FY2012 10-K); DURABLE: no 10-K calls the business cyclical ('cycle' appears only as the sales cycle and payment cycles); no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a subscription software company on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': the 10-K names cloud computing as salesforce.com's own model, the side that displaces on-premise software, not a substitute for it, and names no offshore delivery), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.39x; +143% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.03; conservative 2yr -8%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -25.4%/yr (worst year FY05-FY11 ex-FY07, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +28.1%/yr (Q4 FY13 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 8.5-yr ex-FY07 ex-FY12 median

BULL.desc: EPS +37.4%/yr (FY05-FY11 ex-FY07 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +104.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY05-FY11 ex-FY07, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CRM (retrospective, 2012-12-07) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.39x (87.3% downside to Bear $19.89 / +62.6% upside to Bull $254.81) | Adj composite 1.30 vs market 2.33: gap -1.03 [OVERVALUED] | +143% above the EPP floor $64.39 (137x FY13E $0.47) | Conservative 2-yr case: -7.9% total (-3.9%/yr) | At 333.4x FY13E the 15% hurdle price $207.24 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +34.9% YoY in Q3 FY13, forward revenues +30.6-31.3% (Q4 FY13 revenue guide (Q3 FY13 release)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
